newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo's German registrations up 49.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Volvo's German registrations up 49.8 pct.

text.p: Volvo Cars, a unit of Swedish automotive group AB Volvo, said on Tuesday its German registrations rose by a preliminary 49.8 percent to 3,280 cars in February.
The total market for cars in Germany dropped by 0.6 percent during the same month, Volvo Cars' spokesman Ulf Thorne told Reuters.
Volvo Cars' registrations in Germany rose by 28.1 percent to 5,855 cars during the two first months of 1997, while the total market decreased by 2.1 percent.
Germany is Volvo Cars' fourth biggest market after the U.S., Sweden and Britain.
"The increase in Germany for S40/V40 is sharp this year," Thorne said. "Also S70/V70 has increased compared to the previous 850-series. So far this year the increase is 17 percent."
